discovery: Squeezed states of light and quantum-enhanced interferometric measurement beyond the standard quantum limit
motivation: Caves showed in 1981 that the quantum noise limiting laser interferometers comes from vacuum fluctuations entering the unused port, and that injecting squeezed vacuum could beat the so-called standard quantum limit. Kimble's group gave the first strong demonstrations of quadrature-squeezed light from optical parametric down-conversion (1986), which turned the idea into a working laboratory resource. Schnabel led the development of stable, highly squeezed light sources and their first sustained use in a gravitational-wave observatory, GEO600 (2011). Today squeezed light runs routinely in LIGO, Virgo and KAGRA, and frequency-dependent squeezing raises the detection rate of black-hole and neutron-star mergers by tens of percent. This line of work, running from theory to tabletop experiment to kilometre-scale observatory, showed that a limit long taken as fundamental could be engineered away. Quantum metrology now builds on it, from atomic clocks to dark-matter searches.
